text:
sarah: Heads-up — ACME reported a sudden p99 tail spike on /v1/generate (model=rdx-13b-8k) starting ~2025-09-12T14:22Z. p50 stable, p95 ~2x, p99 ~6x, some 504s. They noticed GPU memory pressure spikes and occasional OOM messages in the worker logs.

kai: Can you paste the tenant id and a short log excerpt? Any recent config/rollouts?

sarah: tenant T-ACME. No config rollouts on their account. Log snippet from affected pod at 14:21:58 UTC:
```
[14:21:57.984] WARN runtime.alloc: allocation retry (evict) failed
[14:21:58.001] ERROR runtime.gpu: GPU OOM while allocating 412MB (attempt 3)
[14:21:58.002] INFO kv.cache: tenant=T-ACME kv_size=328MB entries=12k growth=+40MB/s
[14:21:58.003] WARN runtime.slab: slab_fragmentation=0.78 free=140MB
```

kai: Interesting — logs show repeated allocator retries + high slab fragmentation and KV growth for that tenant. That explains long tail retries that push p99 up.

mike: Agreed. Likely two contributors: (1) KV cache growth for T-ACME holding onto prefixes, (2) slab fragmentation preventing large contiguous allocs => allocator retries and OOM spikes.

olga: Quick mitigations we can try now (low-risk):
- Purge prefix cache for T-ACME via admin API
- Route T-ACME to smaller batch size / lower concurrency on warm pool
- Temporarily enable CPU fallback for their requests if latency allows

sarah: ACME is very sensitive but agreed to a short maintenance window. Can we run purge and reduce batch to 1?

kai: Yes. Purge command:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  "https://admin.redwood.internal/tenants/T-ACME/cache/purge?prefix=all"
```
Then flip route for that tenant to policy=latency-first and max_batch=1:
```json
{"tenant":"T-ACME","route":{"policy":"latency-first","max_batch":1}}
```

deploy-bot: rolling restart started for runtime-pool-7 (pods: runtime-7a, runtime-7b) — triggered by @kai — estimated 3m per pod :arrows_counterclockwise:

mike: After purge + restart, watch these metrics: runtime.slab_fragmentation, runtime.alloc_retries_total, kv.per_tenant_bytes. Use metrics query:
```promql
rate(runtime_alloc_retries_total[1m]) by (tenant)
```

olga: For medium-term: we should tune slab eviction/compaction heuristics and cap per-tenant KV cache. Proposed flags for canary: SLAB_COMPACT_RATIO=0.6, SLAB_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.72, KV_MAX_BYTES_PER_TENANT=268435456 (256MB).

kai: I can push a canary with those env overrides to pool-8 (10% traffic) and monitor p99. Also add a metric for "kv_eviction_count" per tenant.

mike: Add an allocator-level guard to fail fast before attempting >2 eviction rounds — each extra round adds huge tail. Set ALLOC_MAX_EVICT_ROUNDS=2 in the canary.

sarah: ACME approved the immediate purge + batch cap during maintenance. They asked if there's anything else that could help short-term.

kai: Short-term alternatives if pressure remains: (a) route tenant to dedicated capacity (reserved) for a bit, (b) enable active fallback to a smaller quantized variant (rdx-13b-8k-quant) on heavy tails. Both are more disruptive but reduce GPU memory footprint.

mike: Created internal bug: RH-7891 for allocator heuristics + KV caps. Will attach logs and timeline.

olga: After restart+purge, CPU/GPU memory usage on node runtime-7b dropped and slab_fragmentation fell from 0.78 -> 0.56 within ~90s. Eviction count spiked during purge then normalized.

sarah: ACME reports latencies back down to normal after our mitigation. They still want a follow-up on permanent fixes.

kai: Next steps:
- Canary the slab/evict tuning (pool-8) today 10:30 UTC
- Add kv_eviction_count and per-tenant kv_bytes dashboards
- Ship RH-7891 with allocator limits and per-tenant KV caps
- Consider emergency knob to auto-route high-kv tenants to isolated pool

mike: I'll own RH-7891 and run postmortem once we gather canary results. Thanks team :thumbsup:
